question: All of the following factors increases the level of respiratory neuron activity in the medulla, EXCEPT:

options.opb: Rise in H+ concentration of aerial blood

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Rise in PCO2" -> "increased central chemoreceptor activity" -> "increased respiratory neuron activity in medulla" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Rise in H+ concentration of aerial blood" -> "increased central chemoreceptor activity" -> "increased respiratory neuron activity in medulla" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Rise in Po2" -> "possible decreased peripheral chemoreceptor activity" -> "possible decreased respiratory neuron activity in medulla" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Drop in Po2" -> "increased peripheral chemoreceptor activity" -> "increased respiratory neuron activity in medulla" -> 95%
analysis: The medullary respiratory neurons are primarily stimulated by changes in the levels of carbon dioxide (PCO2) and hydrogen ions (H+) in the blood. An increase in PCO2 or H+ concentration leads to increased respiratory neuron activity to expel more CO2 and maintain pH balance. A drop in Po2 can also stimulate respiratory activity, particularly through peripheral chemoreceptors. However, a rise in Po2 does not stimulate respiratory neurons and may actually reduce their activity. Therefore, a rise in Po2 is the exception among the factors listed.
